extra.message: User-controlled filter column names and values are concatenated directly into a raw SQL string (`${col} = '${val}'`) executed via db.execute. A dispatcher/admin can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. UNION, subqueries) to read any table or bypass filters.

The search term (`q`) and sort field (`sort`) are interpolated directly into a raw SQL string (`... ILIKE '%${term}%' ORDER BY ${sortField} ...`) executed via db.execute. Both parameters are user-controlled, enabling SQL injection.

The `format` query parameter is interpolated directly into a shell command (`pandoc ${srcFile} -f html -t ${format} -o ${outFile}`) executed via execAsync. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. `; rm -rf ...`) to execute arbitrary commands.

The `template` query parameter is interpolated into a shell command string passed to spawn with `shell: true` (`wkhtmltopdf --title "${template}" reports/${template}.html ...`). Command injection is possible by injecting shell metacharacters.

The `customFormula` query parameter is passed to `new Function('base','weightKg','distanceKm', 'return (' + q.customFormula + ');')`. This executes arbitrary JavaScript server-side (remote code execution).

The `x-shipment-code` header is embedded unescaped into an XPath predicate (`shipment[@code='${code}']`) which is later evaluated via `new Function` in loadRouteManifest. Allows XPath/code injection and reading arbitrary shipment data.

expandEntities() resolves DOCTYPE-declared SYSTEM entities with `fs.readFileSync(systemPath)`, allowing an attacker-supplied XML manifest to read arbitrary server files (XXE). Reachable via POST /api/routes/:id/carrier-manifest then GET /:id/carrier-manifest/items.

The `x-search-term` header is embedded unescaped into an LDAP filter string (`(cn=*${term}*)`). LDAP filter metacharacters are not escaped, allowing LDAP injection (the by-email handler correctly uses escapeFilter).

The `tag` body field is used directly to build a file path (`path.join(ARCHIVE_DIR, tag + '.csv')`) without basename sanitization, allowing path traversal to write CSV files anywhere the process can access (e.g. ../../ paths).
The `courseName` URL parameter is used unsanitized in `path.join(TRAINING_MATERIALS_DIR, courseName + '.pdf')` and read with fs.readFileSync, allowing path traversal to read arbitrary server files.
The `layout` query parameter is used unsanitized in `path.join(STATEMENT_LAYOUT_DIR, layoutName + '.html')` and read with fs.readFileSync, allowing path traversal to read arbitrary files.

The `kiosk_map_provider` cookie value (set at unauthenticated terminal boot from user-supplied `mapProviderUrl`) is fetched server-side with no host allowlist, enabling SSRF to internal services (e.g. cloud metadata).
The `next_screen` cookie value (user-controlled at boot) is passed directly to `reply.redirect(next)` with no allowlist, enabling open redirect to arbitrary external URLs.

driver-access-assistance never compares the supplied `licenceNumber` to the stored `driverLicenseNumber`. It only checks that the worker has some license on file, then issues a full JWT. Anyone who knows a field worker's email can obtain their token without the license number.

applyRouteSheetCorrection copies every request body field into the job update patch without allowlisting, so a dispatcher can overwrite arbitrary columns (status, assignedWorkerId, regionId, customerId, etc.), bypassing workflow transitions and scoping.

extra.message: resumeJobDraft spreads a user-supplied JSON `draft` object directly into the jobs INSERT values with no schema validation, allowing a dispatcher to set arbitrary columns (status, assignedWorkerId, regionId, reference, etc.).

extra.message: importCustomerProfileSnapshot merges the full request body onto the customer record via Object.assign and updates the DB with no allowlist, allowing an ops admin to overwrite arbitrary customer columns (e.g. creditHoldActive, regionId).

extra.message: syncKioskJobUpdate merges the full request body onto the job record via Object.assign and updates the DB with no allowlist, so a badged-in worker can overwrite arbitrary job fields (status, assignedWorkerId, regionId, customerId, etc.).

extra.message: getJobMessageById loads a message by id and returns it (with sender) without any job access check, unlike every other job handler. Any authenticated user (including customers) can enumerate message ids and read internal messages for other customers' jobs.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: getJobMessageThread trusts the client-supplied `sharingMode` query parameter; a customer can pass `sharingMode=full` to receive the full message thread including internal (customerVisible=false) notes, bypassing the visibility filter.

getCarrierPortalRoutes ignores the carrier account scope and queries `WHERE routes.name = routes.name` (a tautology), returning up to 50 routes for any carrier holding a session. The scoped variant (line 135) has the same flaw. Carriers can enumerate all routes.

extra.message: mergeDeep iterates over all keys of the attacker-controlled overrides object (including `__proto__`/`constructor`) and writes them onto the target without filtering, causing prototype pollution. Reachable via POST /api/board-preferences/sync.

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')

extra.message: Carrier portal account passwords are stored as unsalted SHA-256 hashes (`crypto.createHash('sha256')`). The login handler (line 102) uses the same scheme. Unsalted fast hashes are trivially cracked via rainbow tables/GPU.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: openScopedPortalSession generates carrier portal session tokens as a sequential counter (`cps-${++scopedPortalSequence}`), which is trivially predictable. An attacker can enumerate tokens to hijack any carrier portal session.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: The integration API key falls back to a hardcoded default ('demo-integration-key') when INTEGRATION_API_KEY is unset, allowing unauthenticated callers to push job status changes via the inbound integration endpoint.

replyStagerWidget interpolates the user-controlled message body directly into an HTML onclick attribute with no escaping, then renders it via v-html. A message containing a single quote can break out of the attribute and inject arbitrary script (stored XSS).

getCarrierRateExceptions returns the raw error stack trace to the client in the 502 response body. getCarrierIntegrationHealth similarly leaks error message and stack whenever a client sends an `x-ops-console-session` header.

extra.message: uploadCarrierPortalLogo has no authentication/session check and no MIME or size validation. It derives the extension from the attacker-controlled filename and writes into a public directory, allowing unauthenticated arbitrary file upload.
